title: Two-Track Runway for Hosted API + Model Catalog: Quarterly Plan & Contingency Lanes
creator: Asha Rao
description: Objective: create a two-track quarterly runway that aligns Hosted API demand lanes (performance, price-sensitive, and enterprise) with a model-catalog rotation schedule and explicit contingency triggers. The goal is to reduce surprise migrations mid-quarter by: 1) pre-defining model variants per demand bucket, 2) scheduling staggered canaries and rollbacks tied to perf/cost SLOs, and 3) publishing a lightweight decision playbook for on-call and SEs. This ticket surfaces the milestone plan, acceptance criteria, required engineering tasks, and the cross-functional ramp/rollback triggers. Scope includes: model lineup selection, canary windows, capacity hedging policy, monitoring dashboards, and communication templates for customers and sales.
acceptance_criteria: A1: A prioritized mapping of model variants to three demand lanes (latency-sensitive, cost-sensitive, enterprise-compliant) published and signed off by PM+Research
A2: Canary schedule and automated gate (traffic %, perf delta threshold, cost delta threshold) defined and implemented in the Console routing rules
A3: Two dashboards (model-rotation-heatmap, per-route cost-latency trend) live in Console with per-model annotations and alerting rules
A4: Rollout playbook (step-by-step rollback + communication templates) documented in Confluence and linked from the Console release UI
A5: Dependencies to runtime/infra tasks listed and queued with owners; no critical infra blockers remain before canary windows start
tasks: PM: finalize demand-bucket definitions and map customer cohorts (B2B mid-market, AI-native startups, platform teams)
Research: evaluate top 6 candidate model variants (fp16/quantized/4-bit) for perf/cost tradeoffs and produce benchmarking spreadsheet
ENG: implement canary gating hooks in routing service (traffic % control, perf/cost evaluation window)
ENG: dashboard wiring - expose per-model token-cost, p95 latency, error-rate, and canary annotation via traces
DX/Docs: prepare customer-facing migration playbook and internal runbook with rollback templates
SRE: add synthetic workloads to exercise each demand lane and validate autoscaling/hedge behavior
